If 0 active keepers ever remain on a chain, the RiskModule halts new borrowing and withdrawals with debt on every CDP Spoke of that chain (LiquidationHalted), while liquidation stays open to anyone through the permissionless path. It halts a debt reserve in the same way when some market token has no usable swap route into its asset (DebtLiquidationHalted). Repayment, fee collection and debt-free withdrawal stay open.

Example: Ethereum has keepers K1 and K2. Removing K2 leaves one active keeper and borrowing continues. A removal of K1 then reverts, because it would leave fewer than keeperFloor. If K1's key were compromised, a replacement keeper is added first and K1 is frozen.

The Aave DAO liquidates Avana accounts through LPVaultSwap like anyone else: through the permissionless path from its executor or any address it controls, at once and with no Avana action, or through the keeper path with a keeper address added by the timelock.
After the flash loan and its premium are repaid, the realized surplus is split in a fixed order, all in the debt asset that was repaid:
Avana's fee: 20% of the oracle-value gain of the seizure, never more than the realized surplus. A caller's routing cannot lower it while the realized gain covers it.
Keeper reward: the rest of the oracle-value gain, capped by what was realized. It goes to the caller of either liquidation function.
Borrower surplus: any recovery above the oracle value of the seized collateral, paid to the borrower's wallet.

This fee is Avana's only on-chain revenue. Avana charges no fee on borrow interest. A payout that its recipient cannot receive goes to the payout escrow (InKindEscrow), credited to that recipient, and never reverts the liquidation.
The formulas and the payout order are on the flow page:

Aave reports a deficit inside its liquidation call only when the call empties the account's collateral and debt remains. It then reports the remaining debt of every borrowed reserve, each on its funding Hub and in that reserve's asset, and zeroes the account's debt. Avana accepts this behaviour unchanged. The Avana Umbrella (Coverage Spoke) of each affected Hub and asset covers its deficit within the coverage window, never with another asset's or another Hub's coverage.
A call that reports a deficit settles like any other. If the recovery floor or the funding check fails, the whole transaction reverts, deficit report included.

After a full seizure, every record of the account stays open with 0 credited units. The depositor can collect fees and take the position back with the AaveAdapter's releaseZeroCredit, which needs no debt check. Keepers skip accounts with no collateral left, because Aave has already reported their deficit.

An account with several debt reserves is liquidated by successive calls, one debt reserve each, in the order the keeper chooses. Keepers continue until the health factor is at least 1, when Aave rejects further calls, or a deficit has been recorded.

strings: Welcome
What is Avana?
How It Works
Why LP Collateral Matters
Architecture
Pledge a supported LP position

A borrower pledges an approved Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. A Pledge changes custody but does not remove liquidity from the pool. The position keeps earning fees while it is in range.
Represent and value it

The Collateralization Module mints vault tokens 1:1 with the pledged liquidity. The AaveAdapter supplies them to the market's Avana Borrow Spoke through the borrower's Position Proxy. The LPOracle values each vault token from the pool's liquidity math at Chainlink prices, with no haircut. It then checks the result against the pool's TWAP.
Borrow GHO from the Avana Hub

Borrowing capacity is the position's value multiplied by the reserve's Collateral Factor. If capacity is sufficient, the borrower draws GHO from the Avana Hub. A capped GHO credit line from the Aave DAO funds the Hub.
Liquidity stays in the pool

Pledging an LP position moves custody to the LP Vault but leaves its liquidity in the underlying pool. The borrower can borrow GHO without first withdrawing the position and giving up its fees or range.
Valuation and limits are separate
The LPOracle reports the value of the liquidity with no haircut. Each reserve's Collateral Factor, min(Token0CF, Token1CF) × PoolRiskFactor, sets how much of that value supports debt.
Liquidation has explicit rules

Each market has an approved settlement mode. LPVaultSwap uses a flash loan to repay debt and settle the LP collateral in one transaction. Partial settlement removes only the liquidity needed to restore health. Full-position settlement settles the whole position and returns any surplus to the borrower.
Introduction
Avana lets liquidity providers borrow GHO on Aave V4 against their Uniswap v2 and v3 positions. The positions stay active in their pools and keep earning trading fees.
Start with Key Concepts
Explore Borrow Spoke

Avana brings AMM liquidity positions to Aave V4 as collateral. A depositor pledges a Uniswap v2 LP token or Uniswap v3 position to the LP Vault. The depositor then borrows GHO from the Avana Hub while the position stays in the pool.
To borrow against LP assets elsewhere, a liquidity provider usually has to withdraw from the pool first. Withdrawing gives up trading fees and, for concentrated positions, the chosen range.

Avana keeps the position in its pool. The LP Vault holds the position, and a vault token represents it on an Avana Borrow Spoke. A vault token is a transfer-restricted, collateral-only ERC-20 record that maps 1:1 to the underlying liquidity. Avana runs on Ethereum mainnet with selected Uniswap v2 and v3 markets.

Each stage connects a user action to the protocol's accounting. A Pledge establishes custody. Valuation and the Collateral Factor determine borrowing capacity. A borrow creates GHO debt against that capacity. The following guides explain each step in detail.

LP collateral lets assets already deployed in an AMM support a GHO loan. The benefit is capital flexibility, not guaranteed positive carry. Borrowers still bear impermanent loss, price risk and liquidation risk.

The Avana Hub and Avana Borrow Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO. All Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts: LP Vault, AaveAdapter, LPOracle, RiskModule, CollateralizationModule, LPVaultSwap, AMMSettlementAdapters and AvanaConfig.

Each market category (Stable LP, Correlated LP and Blue-chip/stable LP) has its own Avana Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps. The Avana Hub holds the GHO credit line, and only approved Borrow Spokes can draw from it. A dedicated Position Proxy holds each borrower's Aave position. Deposits, borrows, repayments and withdrawals therefore pass through Avana's controls. The Avana Lend Spoke lets lenders supply assets directly to the Avana Hub. Aave governance approves it separately.

Contracts & Security
The contract set, its upgradeability and ownership, and the review status of Avana's code.

Avana does not fork, copy or modify Aave V4 code. The Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes are standard Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO. All Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts. The design follows the pattern of Babylon's native BTC integration on Aave V4.

Security review covers both contract execution and economic behavior. A valid contract call can still produce a wrong lending result if its price input is stale or its settlement route cannot execute. For this reason, oracle checks and in-transaction settlement are part of the design. Contract names may change after audits.
• LP positions are not ERC-20 reserves. Avana keeps custody in the LP Vault, separate from the vault tokens that represent positions on Aave. Every vault token must stay backed.

• Stale or manipulated prices can cause loss even when contracts execute as coded. LPOracle therefore uses Chainlink as the reference price, the pool TWAP as a consistency check, and maximum feed ages.
• Upgrades, pause and freeze roles, and configuration are privileged controls and part of the attack surface.
Internal security review
Core contracts and the Aave V4 integration are feature-complete and in internal security review, including AI-assisted analysis.
Technical and risk assessment
A technical and risk assessment with Aave DAO service providers covers position custody, valuation, liquidation, the Aave V4 integration, governance roles, loss allocation and economic terms.
Independent audits
Independent public audits follow the internal review, and their reports are published. The
Bug Bounty
page describes the disclosure scope. Program terms are announced separately.

• Vault tokens have no owner or admin. They can be transferred only to the Avana Hub, Borrow Spokes, Position Proxies, Aave Adapter and LPVaultSwap. They are minted only on approved deposit and burned on withdrawal or settlement.
• Chainlink feeds, AMM TWAPs, the GHO FlashMinter and CoW Swap are external dependencies whose failure can affect valuation or recovery.

• Upgrades go through a timelock that Avana Labs cannot bypass, and the Aave DAO can cancel them. The Aave DAO holds pause and freeze roles over Avana's contracts. The Emergency Guardian can pause, freeze and cancel, but cannot upgrade, change parameters or move collateral.
The public sandbox at app.avana.cc uses simulated assets and makes no onchain transactions. It is not evidence of production readiness.
Changes to supported AMMs, settlement routes, oracle models or privileged roles change the audit scope, because they change how collateral is admitted, valued or settled.

How first-loss capital, committed revenues and Avana Umbrella cover losses in Avana's Aave V4 markets.
Avana covers losses in three layers: dedicated first-loss capital, then revenues committed to loss coverage, then Avana Umbrella. Avana Umbrella is Avana's protocol safety module, named after
Aave Umbrella
. Collateral limits and liquidation remain the first controls against loss. Coverage is limited to the capital actually funded and committed. It is not a guarantee for every position.

If liquidation proceeds do not cover the debt being repaid, LPVaultSwap draws from the FirstLossReserve in the same transaction. If the reserve cannot cover the shortfall, the transaction reverts and debt and collateral are unchanged. Keepers may retry with a smaller partial liquidation. Borrowing is activated only once a process for resolving such positions is in place.

Aave V4 records a deficit on the Avana Hub only when a completed standard Aave V4 liquidation uses up an account's collateral with debt remaining. A liquidation that reverts does not create a deficit, and the debt stays on the account. The Avana Hub is a standard Aave V4 contract owned by the Aave DAO. Only approved Borrow Spokes have GHO draw capacity on it.

The first layer is dedicated first-loss capital held in the FirstLossReserve contract. Its size is set with Aave DAO service providers. The reserve counts toward coverage only once it is funded. A commitment alone is not coverage.
LPVaultSwap draws on the FirstLossReserve directly during liquidation, so first-loss capital is used before any deficit reaches the Avana Hub. Avana's monthly reports include first-loss resources.
Losses are absorbed in a fixed order. Each layer is used before the next.
1. Dedicated first-loss capital (FirstLossReserve) 2. Revenues committed to loss coverage 3. Avana Umbrella

The size of each layer, and which revenues are committed to loss coverage, are set with Aave DAO service providers and approved by governance. All interest revenue attributable to the GHO credit line accrues to the Aave DAO.

A shortfall found during liquidation is covered from the FirstLossReserve in the same transaction, or the liquidation reverts. A deficit recorded on the Avana Hub after a completed standard liquidation is covered in the loss order above.

The Aave DAO's exposure is limited to the capped GHO credit line. Each increase to the credit line requires governance approval. Governance defines the exact settlement steps for covering a Hub deficit.

Avana Umbrella is the third layer of the loss order and is named after Aave's Umbrella. Its mechanics are not specified yet, including which assets can be staked, reward terms, slashing limits and withdrawal cooldowns. A separate governance approval sets them. Aave v3 Umbrella token addresses, cooldowns and parameters are not defaults for Avana.

The GHO credit line grows in stages. Each stage has its own conditions and requires governance approval. Only funded capital counts as protection, and amounts spent during liquidation are deducted from available coverage. Coverage applies to GHO deficits on the Avana Hub. Weekly usage reports and monthly revenue reports let readers check coverage against exposure. The reports include bad debt, FirstLossReserve usage, credit-line usage and first-loss resources. They also include successful, failed and retried liquidations.

Loss coverage applies to protocol shortfalls and deficits. It does not reimburse borrowers, who still bear impermanent loss, price risk and liquidation risk. Coverage is limited to capital actually available. It does not increase borrowing capacity or remove liquidation risk. Risk Framework
How governance roles, the upgrade timelock and emergency controls apply to the Avana Hub, Borrow Spokes and Avana's own contracts.

The Avana Hub and Borrow Spokes are standard, unmodified Aave V4 contracts owned by the Aave DAO. Avana-specific logic sits in Avana's own contracts: the LP Vault, AvanaConfig, Risk Module, Collateralization Module, LPOracle, AMM settlement adapters, Aave Adapter and LPVaultSwap.

Avana has three pool categories: stable, correlated and blue-chip/stable. Each category has its own Borrow Spoke, parameters and caps. Each market also has its own pool risk factor, settlement mode and oracle settings.

Three parties hold separate powers: the Aave DAO, Avana Labs and an Emergency Guardian multisig. Avana Labs submits and administers changes, and a designated risk reviewer reviews them. The Aave DAO approves changes and can stop markets. The Guardian can only pause, freeze and cancel.
Operating rule:
the Aave DAO can pause, freeze or stop Avana markets without Avana Labs, and Avana Labs cannot bypass the upgrade timelock.

Limits on emergency powers
Emergency powers can only stop or restrict activity. Borrowers can still repay and make permitted withdrawals by calling the contracts directly, without Avana's frontend.

Avana Labs owns, operates and pays for its own contracts, audits, monitoring and keepers. The Aave DAO's exposure is limited to the capped GHO credit line. Each increase to the credit line requires governance approval.
